 Judgment
This appeal is by the claimants in MVC No.174/2015 on the file of the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT- VII, Vijayapura [for short, 'the Tribunal'].

The appellant's claim petition is disposed of by the impugned judgment and award dated 03.08.2018 granting a total compensation of Rs.2,04,400/- under the following heads:
 Pain and sufferings Rs.30,000/-
 Future medical expenses, attendant, Rs.14,000/-
 conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental expenses (Medical + Future attendant charges) Loss of income during laid-up Rs.5,000/- period NC: 2023:KHC-K:1113-DB Loss of future income on account of Rs.1,40,400/-
permanent disability Loss of amenities, life comforts and Rs.15,000/- expectancy of life Total Rs.2,04,400/-
2.
Sri Koujalagi Chandrakant Laxman and Sri S.S. Aspalli, the learned counsels for the appellant and the respondents, are heard for final disposal of the appeal.

The appellant is aggrieved by the award Yamanappa vs Rajanna H.T And Anr on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105598280/

sentences.text: 3. It is undisputed that the appellant has suffered facial injuries when he was traveling in the bus insured by the second respondent.
The Disability Certificate dated 01.08.2017 issued by Mahantesh Multi Speciality Hospital, Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre, Ilkal remains undisputed, and this certificate is marked as Ex.P-16.

entities.text: Mahantesh Multi Speciality Hospital, Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre, Ilkal
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is seen from this Certificate that the appellant, who is a professional Shahanai player, has suffered multiple fractures involving right orbital floor, lateral wall of right orbit, right zygomatic arch, medial wall of right maxillary sinus and he is advised to undergo physiotherapy for a period of three weeks.

The NC: 2023:KHC-K:1113-DB award of a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards pain and suffering in the light of the injuries suffered, and the appellant's profession, would be very conservative and there must be appropriate enhancement in that regard.

4. Though Sri Koujalagi Chandrakant Laxman argues that there must be enhancement in compensation towards loss of future earning capacity because the appellant is a professional Shahanai player, the Wound Certificate and the Disability Certificate indicate that the injuries have by themselves not resulted in any functional disability.

Hence, there cannot be increase in the award under the loss of future income because of permanent disability, but, as aforesaid, it cannot be gainsaid that with multiple fractures with advice for physiotherapy thereafter for a period of three weeks, there must be a just and reasonable compensation towards pain and suffering especially because the appellant is a Shahanai player whose earning capacity would be disrupted for some time.

In the circumstances of the case where only a sum of Rs.30,000/- and Rs.15,000/- are awarded respectively towards pain and NC: 2023:KHC-K:1113-DB suffering and loss of amenities,
there must be a further compensation.
This Court is of the considered view that a global sum of Rs.1,00,000/- would be just and appropriate.

Hence, the appeal stands disposed of by the following:
ORDER

The judgment and award by the Tribunal dated 03.08.2018 in MVC No.174/2015 is modified granting to the appellant a global sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
calling upon the second respondent to deposit the said amount with the Tribunal for disbursement within a period of eight [8] weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
